newsitem.title: USA: Pass commodity law reform in early 97-US Sen Lugar.
newsitem.headline: Pass commodity law reform in early 97-US Sen Lugar.

text.p: Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar said Wednesday that he hoped to see passage in early 1997 of revisions to the basic U.S. law governing commodity traders.
"This is something we would try to achieve in the first quarter of the year," Lugar said in a interview with Reuters.

On attempts for an agreement over how to interpret the so-called Treasury Amendment, which exempted interbank foreign-exchange trading from Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Lugar wants to include consensus language on the issue in his Commodity Exchange Act reforms.

Lugar, Indiana Republican, and Vermont Senator Patrck Leahy, the panel's Democratic leader, planed to re-introduce in January a bill to ease regulations on futures exchanges and to give the CFTC more power over foreign futures contracts that allow U.S. delivery.

CFTC and the Treasury have tried for months to resolve ambiguities in the 1974 Treasury Amendment. The Supreme Court was scheduled to hear a case on the matter next week. A ruling was not expected until next year.
Efforts also were being made to achieve consensus between the administration and the private sector.

An aide to Lugar said it was hoped the administration could report progress or even a consensus on the issue by the end of this year. Such a step could provide a basis for language that would go into the Lugar-Leahy bill.

Prompt action should be possible next year, Lugar said, because a draft version of the bill was filed in August. Commodity exchanges have commented on the proposed changes, he said, and he has conferred with CFTC leaders.
